doc.name: A — whisky catalogue, water reflection, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: single-malt bottle and rocks glass
Category: whisky
Shot programme: water reflection
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this whisky product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the in-context lifestyle in a water reflection treatment.

SUBJECT. A single-malt bottle and rocks glass. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Product in its real use environment with lived-in supporting props. Shoot on a 90mm tilt-shift at f/1.4, framing for a shallow out-of-focus foreground element occluding the lower third.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with scrim-diffused midday daylight, one stop under the ambient. Stage the product on or against raw board-formed concrete, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
